source.title: Junior School Curriculum Design: Islamic Religious Education, Grade 9
source.notes: Filename confirmed against KICD's own Google Drive listing (kicd.ac.ke/cbc-materials/curriculum-designs/grade-nine-designs/, file id 1QAtDW4Pq0enTVPOb32TlfQzge2au4RRC, whose /preview page title reads 'Islamic Religious Education Grade 9 - July 2024.pdf'). WebFetch reported it could not extract text from the PDF but saved it locally; Read then parsed the full PDF text natively (ISBN 978-9914-43-435-4, First Published 2024). Strand/sub-strand headings, SLOs, and key inquiry questions below are transcribed verbatim. CAVEAT: strand 6.0 (Muamalat) includes sensitive real-world sub-strands (domestic violence, polygamy, Zina/prohibitions, terrorism and extremism) exactly as the official curriculum frames them — these are legitimate, officially mandated Grade 9 IRE content, not editorial additions, and should be built as the design presents them (Islamic teaching/rules on the topic) rather than reframed or softened.

subStrands.name: Ulum al-Qur'an
subStrands.notes: The miraculous nature of the Qur'an, language of the Qur'an, styles of the Qur'an.
specificLearningOutcomes: Describe the miraculous nature of the Qur'an to strengthen iman
Explain the language of the Qur'an for better understanding
Identify different styles of the Qur'an for better understanding
Appreciate the miraculous nature of the Qur'an as a divine scripture
keyInquiryQuestions: Why is the Qur'an considered a miracle?
How does the language and style of the Qur'an help in its interpretation?

subStrands.name: Selected Chapter Surah Al-Hujurat (Q 49)
specificLearningOutcomes: Read Surah al-Hujurat (Q 49) correctly for spiritual nourishment
Explain the meaning of the verses of Surah al-Hujurat for better understanding
Deduce lessons from Surah al-Hujurat for application in daily life
Apply the teachings of Surah al-Hujurat in their daily life
Treasure the teachings from Surah al-Hujurat as a guide in relationships
keyInquiryQuestions: What do Muslims learn from Surah al-Hujurat?
How can Muslims use Surah al-Hujurat to enhance peace in the community?

subStrands.name: Ulum al-Hadith
subStrands.notes: Books of Hadith, classification of Hadith (sahih, hasan, dhaif), collection and compilation of Hadith (Tabi'in and Tabi'i-Tabi'in).
specificLearningOutcomes: Identify the six authentic Books of Hadith as a source of guidance
Describe the characteristics of different classes of Hadith (sahih, hasan, and dhaif) to differentiate between authentic and unauthentic Hadith
Explain reasons for the classification of Hadith for authenticity
Examine factors that necessitated the collection and compilation of Hadith during the period of Tabi'in and Tabi'i-Tabi'in as a measure of preservation
Describe the process of collection and compilation of Hadith during the period of the Tabi'in and Tabi'i-Tabi'in to authenticate Hadith
Appreciate the collection and compilation of Hadith as a source of Islamic sharia
keyInquiryQuestions: Why was it important to collect and compile Hadith?
Why is Hadith classified?

subStrands.name: Selected Hadith
subStrands.notes: Hadith on Unity (Muslim: the similitude of believers as one body) and Hadith on Avoidance of ill motives (Bukhari: beware of suspicion).
specificLearningOutcomes: Deduce lessons from the Hadith on unity and avoidance of ill motives among Muslims
Explain the relevance of the Hadith on unity and avoidance of ill motives in the life of a Muslim
Practise the teachings from the Hadith on unity and avoidance of ill motives in daily life
Honour Hadith as the second source of law and spiritual guidance
keyInquiryQuestions: Why is the unity of Muslims important?
Why should Muslims avoid ill motives?

subStrands.name: Belief in the Last Day (Day of Judgement)
subStrands.notes: Resurrection, gathering, record of deeds, scale of deeds, accounting, intercession, siraat, paradise, and hellfire.
specificLearningOutcomes: Describe the events of the Last Day for accountability
Assess the significance of believing in the Last Day for spiritual nourishment
Exercise righteousness in preparation for the Last Day
Desire to lead a righteous life to earn Allah (S.W.T.)'s blessings
keyInquiryQuestions: Why is it important for Muslims to believe in the Last Day?

subStrands.name: Belief in Qadar
specificLearningOutcomes: Describe the effects of believing in Qadar and Qadha as a pillar of Iman
Assess the significance of believing in Qadar and Qadha for spiritual nourishment
Appreciate belief in Qadar and Qadha to accept the Will of Allah
keyInquiryQuestions: Why should Muslims believe in Qadar and Qadha?

subStrands.name: Shariah (Islamic law)
subStrands.notes: Maqasid al-Shariah: protection of religion, intellect, life, property, and dignity.
specificLearningOutcomes: Explain the purpose of Islamic Shariah (Maqasid al-Shariah) as a guide for Muslims
Assess the relevance of Islamic Shariah in the contemporary world
Describe the categories of legal acts in Islamic Shariah as a means of upholding divine guidance
Apply Islamic Shariah in day-to-day life
Acknowledge Shariah as a source of divine guidance
keyInquiryQuestions: What is the objective of Maqasid Shariah?
How do legal acts guide Muslims?

subStrands.name: Tawbah (Repentance)
specificLearningOutcomes: State the conditions of tawbah as a basis for forgiveness from Allah (S.W.T.)
Assess the significance of tawbah in the life of a Muslim
Practise actions that lead to tawbah as a way of purifying one from sins
Appreciate the virtue of tawbah as a condition for success in this life and the Hereafter
keyInquiryQuestions: Why should a Muslim seek repentance from Allah (S.W.T.)?
How should Muslims seek repentance from Allah (S.W.T.)?

subStrands.name: Virtues in Islam
specificLearningOutcomes: Explain Islamic teachings on observing modesty, contentment, and trustworthiness in fulfilment of Allah (S.W.T.)'s commandments
Describe ways in which Muslims can practise modesty, contentment, and trustworthiness as part of faith
Assess the significance of observing modesty, contentment and trustworthiness in upholding Islamic morality in society
Practise modesty, contentment, and trustworthiness in day-to-day life to earn rewards from Allah (S.W.T.)
Value modesty, contentment, and trustworthiness for a morally upright society
keyInquiryQuestions: Why is it important for Muslims to practise virtues?
How can a Muslim student exercise contentment in his life?

subStrands.name: Significance of Islamic Morality
specificLearningOutcomes: Assess the significance of Islamic morality in promoting righteousness
Practise Islamic morality to earn Allah's rewards
Uphold Islamic morality as a way of promoting an upright society
keyInquiryQuestions: Why is it important to uphold Islamic morality?

subStrands.name: Prohibitions in Islam
subStrands.notes: Zina (fornication and adultery) — its effects, the rationale for prohibition, and Islamic measures for curbing it.
specificLearningOutcomes: Describe the effects of Zina on the community
Justify the reasons behind the prohibition of Zina for a morally upright society
Explain the Islamic measures of curbing Zina for a morally upright society
Appreciate the prohibition of Zina for a healthy society
keyInquiryQuestions: Why is Zina prohibited in Islam?
How can a Muslim discourage Zina in the society?

subStrands.name: Domestic violence
specificLearningOutcomes: Explain the causes of domestic violence to settle family conflicts
Explain the effects of domestic violence on the family
Describe measures to curb domestic violence in the family
Embrace measures proposed by Islam to curb domestic violence
keyInquiryQuestions: What are the causes of domestic violence?
How does domestic violence hinder social harmony?

subStrands.name: Iddah
subStrands.notes: The waiting period observed by a divorcee or widow in Islam.
specificLearningOutcomes: Describe the iddah for a divorcee and a widow in Islam to foster obedience to divine guidance
Explain the rationale for observing iddah as an act of ibadah
State the rules of iddah as a means of safeguarding its validity
Assess the importance of iddah to the divorced and widowed Muslim woman
Appreciate iddah as an act of ibadah
keyInquiryQuestions: What is the wisdom behind Iddah?

subStrands.name: Child custody
specificLearningOutcomes: Identify the Islamic rules on child custody to safeguard the child's rights
Assess the significance of Islamic rules on child custody
Appreciate Islamic teachings on child custody as a means of fostering family bonds
keyInquiryQuestions: What are the rules that guide child custody in Islam?

subStrands.name: Polygamy in Islam
specificLearningOutcomes: Explain the reasons for polygamy in Islam for social stability
Justify the reasons for the Prophet's multiple marriages
State the conditions for polygamy in Islam
Assess the significance of polygamy in Islam
Appreciate the Islamic concept of polygamy as a social remedy to safeguard human dignity
keyInquiryQuestions: What is the rationale for polygamy in Islam?

subStrands.name: Trade and Finance in Islam
subStrands.notes: Rules on borrowing/lending money and the role of consumer protection agencies.
specificLearningOutcomes: Explain the Islamic rules on borrowing and lending money
Practise Islamic teachings on borrowing and lending money to earn rewards from Allah (S.W.T.)
Describe the role of consumer protection agencies in enhancing integrity
Appreciate the Islamic concept of borrowing and lending money as a means of safeguarding equity in society
keyInquiryQuestions: Why should Muslims observe the rules of borrowing and lending money?

subStrands.name: Contemporary Issues
specificLearningOutcomes: Identify the rules of Jihad in Islam for a correct interpretation
Explain the causes of terrorism and extremism in the society
Explain the effects of terrorism and extremism on the society
Describe the measures to curb terrorism and extremism for peaceful co-existence
Acknowledge Islamic teachings on Jihad as a guide to harmonious co-existence
keyInquiryQuestions: What are the effects of terrorism and extremism?
How can terrorism and extremism be curbed?

subStrands.name: Islam in Kenya
subStrands.notes: Spread of Islam across Coast, Western, Central, and North Eastern Kenya.
specificLearningOutcomes: Describe the factors that facilitated the spread of Islam in Kenya
Explain the effects of the contact between the early Muslims and the natives as a factor of civilisation
Examine the challenges faced by the early Muslims in the propagation of Islam
Appreciate the contribution of Islam to the development of culture in Kenya
keyInquiryQuestions: What factors facilitated the spread of Islam in Kenya?
What was the impact of the contact between the early Muslims and the natives?

subStrands.name: Unity of Muslims
specificLearningOutcomes: Explain the factors that would enhance the unity of Muslims in Kenya
Describe the challenges that undermine the unity of Muslims in Kenya
Assess the significance of the unity of Muslims for harmonious co-existence
Practise acts that foster unity among Muslims
Appreciate the unity of Muslims to enhance brotherhood
keyInquiryQuestions: Why is the unity of Muslims important?
What hinders the unity of Muslims?

subStrands.name: Muslim Institutions
specificLearningOutcomes: Describe the role of mosques, madrasa, and Muslim NGOs in the preservation of Islamic heritage
Examine the challenges facing the Muslim institutions
Propose possible solutions to the challenges facing Muslim institutions
Recognise the role played by mosques, madrasa, and Muslim NGOs in preserving Islamic values
keyInquiryQuestions: Why are mosques and madrasa important to the Muslim community?
